sonnet.problem: "Not a remodel, friend" takes a side on what the new heavens and new earth are, replacement or renewal. The text only says "I will create new heavens and a new earth," and that picture is debated.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so. His jokes don't take a side on a debated phrase either.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word from the verse. Nothing earlier tells what the ox eats, so "straw" cannot be reasoned out. "Leaves" is also arguably right, since an ox could be said to eat leaves.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: "I'll let that one stand on its own" is Papa Dorin commenting on how he is telling the passage.
sonnet.rule: He talks as "I" and never comments on how he tells the passage.
